source.name: api.quran.com v4
source.note: Arabic and translation are verbatim from the API, as the app itself fetches them.

audio.note: Left channel of the source, which is exactly dual mono (the L-R difference measures -91 dB), trimmed from 1.12s to 27.90s. highpass 70 Hz, +1.6 dB, then a true-peak limiter at -2.0 dBFS: -12.0 LUFS with LRA 5.8 preserved of the dry 6.0. Left undenoised on purpose — the noise floor measures p5 -28.3 dB, marginally quieter than the Maryam reel's -26.6 dB, so there is nothing here that reel did not already have.

timing.method: Boundaries were read off the sound, not guessed. A 5 ms envelope gives the quiet troughs; each candidate slice was then transcribed on its own and had to come back as exactly one ayah. 1.40-4.90 returns 'wa-sayujannabuha l-atqa' and nothing more; 4.90-9.70 returns 18 entire; 9.70-18.37 returns 19 entire.

verses.english: But the righteous one will avoid it
[He] who gives [from] his wealth to purify himself

verses.arabic: وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِندَهُۥ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰٓ
verses.english: And not [giving] for anyone who has [done him] a favor to be rewarded
But only seeking the face [i.e., acceptance] of his Lord, Most High.
And he is going to be satisfied.

marks.note: enMark is the English counterpart of each ayah's closing rhyme word; the Arabic rhyme is the final token, found at build time. In al-Layl the rhyme IS the argument — al-atqa, yatazakka, tujza, al-a'la, yarda — so every one of the five is marked.

onsets.note: When he reaches the rhyme word, from word-level transcription, less the trim.
